chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from al-Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) said:

I asked him about a man who sold a slave and found wealth belonging to him. He said: 'The wealth belongs to the seller; he only sold his person, unless he stipulated that whatever wealth or belongings he had belong to him.'
ai.seo_question: Does selling a slave include their personal wealth and belongings?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifying that a slave's personal wealth (*mal*) remains with the seller by default, as the sale pertains primarily to the person (*nafs*). This principle highlights the distinct legal status of a slave's acquired property in Shia jurisprudence, which can be transferred only if explicitly stipulated (*shart*) in the contract. It underscores the flexibility of contractual conditions in determining the scope of ownership transfer.
